summary: The agent implemented nearly all inherited-super-mapping behavior and preserved all baseline functionality, but one new test failed because a three-way incomparable-branch conflict diagnostic named only the first two declaring mapper types instead of every competing type.
quick_failure_summary: A three-way inherited mapping conflict diagnostic omits the third declaring mapper type.

details.reasoning: The implementation records one inherited mapping per target and, after detecting the first incomparable pair, removes that mapping and marks the target as conflicting. Later declarations for that target are skipped, so a third incomparable branch is never included in the diagnostic. The hidden suite passed 102 of 103 new tests and all 3649 baseline tests, isolating the defect to conflict aggregation rather than the broader feature or its integration.
details.secondary_factors: The agent's own diagnostic fixture covered only a two-branch conflict, so targeted validation did not expose the three-or-more branch case.

justification.issue_description: Conflict diagnostics for a target inherited from three or more incomparable branches must identify every competing declaring mapper type, but the implementation reports only the first pair.
justification.evidence: The prompt states that competing mappings for the same target are a compilation error that identifies the target and declaring mapper types. Java mapper interfaces can extend an arbitrary number of parent interfaces, so collecting all incomparable declarations is a foreseeable consequence of that requirement. In MethodRetrievalProcessor, conflictingTargets causes subsequent mappings for the already-conflicting target to be skipped; the failing diagnostic consequently names ThreeWayAlphaK7p4 and ThreeWayBetaK7p4 but omits ThreeWayGammaK7p4.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT rather than a test mismatch or undocumented edge case because the visible prompt requires identifying the declaring mapper types involved in the competition, not merely one conflicting pair. A competent implementation should retain and diagnose the full set of most-specific incomparable declarations.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is broad and processor-heavy but solvable, as demonstrated by the reference solution and the agent passing nearly the entire comprehensive suite. The three-way diagnostic expectation follows reasonably from the stated conflict rule.

evidence: JUnit reports show 3649 of 3649 baseline tests passed and 102 of 103 new tests passed.
The sole failure is a deterministic assertion on the diagnostic text produced by agent-modified conflict-handling code.
The trajectory shows that rg was unavailable, but the agent immediately switched to find/grep and continued implementation and validation successfully.
The agent completed targeted tests and checkstyle without API, dependency, permission, runtime, or bootstrap failures.
The post-agent harness reported a test.patch merge recovery step, but it successfully executed all 103 new tests, so that did not block or distort the result.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker was found; the single failing test is explained by incomplete conflict-diagnostic aggregation in the implementation.
